question: Which of the following elements is extracted by electrolysis reduction?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Na**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sodium (Na)** is extracted by electrolysis of molten sodium chloride (NaCl).
 
• The process is known as the **Downs process**, where molten sodium chloride is electrolyzed.
 
• During electrolysis, sodium ions are reduced at the cathode to form sodium metal.
 
• Sodium is highly reactive and cannot be extracted by simple reduction methods, necessitating the use of electrolysis.
 
• Electrolysis is crucial for extracting highly reactive metals like sodium from their compounds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electrolysis Process**

 
 
• Electrolysis involves passing an electric current through a molten or aqueous solution to cause a chemical change.
 
• It is widely used for extracting metals from their ores and purifying them.
 
• The process is performed in an electrolytic cell, which consists of two electrodes: an anode and a cathode.
 
• During electrolysis, cations move towards the cathode to gain electrons (reduction), and anions move towards the anode to lose electrons (oxidation).
 
 
 
• **Downs Process**
 
 
• This process is specifically used for the extraction of sodium metal from molten sodium chloride.
 
• It involves the use of a carbon anode and an iron cathode in a molten sodium chloride bath.
 
• Sodium is collected at the cathode, while chlorine gas is produced at the anode.
 
• Calcium chloride is often added to lower the melting point of sodium chloride in this process.
 
 
 
• **Reactivity Series**
 
 
• The reactivity series is a list of elements ordered by their reactivity.
 
• Sodium is placed high in the reactivity series, indicating its high reactivity.
 
• Highly reactive metals like sodium cannot be extracted by simple chemical reduction methods.
 
• Electrolysis is necessary for extracting these metals from their compounds.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Sodium**
 
 
• Sodium is used in various industrial processes, including the manufacture of sodium compounds and in the reduction of metals.
 
• It is also used in street lighting and as a heat exchanger in some nuclear reactors.
 
• Sodium compounds, such as sodium chloride and sodium hydroxide, have numerous applications in industries and households.
